what.summary: Analyzed four candidate paths for the FROST library decision that gates Phase A of the FROST-first quorum + charter-governance roadmap. Surfaced an internal contradiction in the 2026-05-25 brief: operator-locked decision #1 names Rust→WASM but the candidate table immediately below presents two pure-TS options and labels the choice 'deferred to Phase A.' Recommended Path 1 (@cmdcode/frost as pure-TS dep) if decision #1 is reopen-able, Path 2 (Rust→WASM zcash/frost-secp256k1) if it stands as written. Ruled out Path 3 (@frosts/secp256k1-tr — alpha) and Path 4 (vendor cmdcode/frost source — extra burden for no safety improvement vs Path 1). Closing with a chip-form question to lock the path.

why.text: Operator asked for the best Phase A implementation path with full analysis of each option. The brief explicitly anticipates this evaluation as Phase A's first sub-task. The chip-form lock unblocks the actual cut.

outcome.notes: [P-001] read brief in full and traced operator-locked decisions. [P-002] surveyed live npm registry for FROST candidates (cmdcode, @frosts/secp256k1-tr, @toruslabs/tss-frost-client, @substrate-system/frost-dkg, @bcts/frost-hubert). [P-003] corrected brief's frostlib reference (does not exist on npm). [P-004] flagged internal contradiction between decision #1 prose and candidate table. [P-005] delivered four-path comparison with recommendation. [P-006] asked chip-form lock question per PFOR-019. Gates not run — no source-tree changes this session. [FEEDBACK→Foreman]: when a brief locks a decision in prose and re-opens it in a sub-table, the contradiction is invisible until someone reads to act on it. A brief-lint sweep that flags 'locked' + 'deferred' co-occurrence in the same section would catch this earlier.

confidence.uncertainty: Bundle-size estimate for @cmdcode/frost (40–60KB gz post-treeshake) is the brief's number, not a measured one. Confirming requires installing the package and running a probe build. Worth doing before Phase A's actual cut, not before the chip-form decision.

next: Operator picks Path 1 / Path 2 / something else via the chip-form question. On lock, write a new decisions.md entry (D-12 or next available) recording the FROST library choice plus rationale, then cut Phase A's first commit: add the dep, scaffold the adapter, write the RFC 9591 vector test, bump tapit-attest version, run all four gates.
